engagement_title: Coble & Vane cask release: reduce a full-colour illustrated mark to a one-ink system that survives wax, stencil and cap, rebuild the printer's die sheet into a live twelve-cask run, and hand back the supplier sheet editable
vertical: Spirits & Craft Manufacturing (two-person coastal distillery, Northumberland, England, shop-direct plus roughly forty independent merchants)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork product-packaging brief behind this ledger slot, a trading firm launching its first private-label line that needed an approved master logo extended into a working variant system, swappable per-SKU labels and single-colour cartons built as data-driven templates, plus a digital asset pack for suppliers. Laundered to a fictional coined brand, Coble & Vane; no real company, product, person or trademark is named. The ledger verdict was REBUILD, because as banked the concept sat on one surface: trace the logo, hand back four SVGs. A supplier-facing mark system is judged on the stamped and printed objects it lands on, and the client who commissions one almost always has a packaging run in flight and a printer holding the only copy of last year's artwork. VECTOR-08 restores that commission: a colour illustration that has to become one ink, a die sheet nobody at the distillery has opened, twelve cask releases needing labels, and a supplier sheet that has to stay editable.
client_one_liner: Twelve cask releases, one mark that only exists in full colour, and almost nothing we print is in colour, so the mark, the labels and the sheet that tells suppliers what to do all have to come back from one person before bottling starts.
client_brief:
Coble & Vane, cask release: the mark in one ink, this year's release labels, and a sheet that tells a supplier how to use them.

We are a two-person distillery on the Northumberland coast. Iris runs the still, I run everything else. Twelve cask releases a year, sold from the shop and through about forty independent merchants, bottles fifty-five to a hundred and twenty dollars.

Our mark was drawn for us six years ago by an illustrator who has since moved abroad. It is beautiful, it is in full colour, and it is very little use to us, because almost nothing we print is in colour. The wax on the bottle neck is one ink. The crate stencil is one ink. The cap is one ink. The shoulder emboss is not ink at all. Every time a supplier asks for a single-colour version, somebody here opens the colour file, does something to it and sends whatever comes out. No two have ever matched.

So, first: give us our mark in one ink, in whatever versions it genuinely needs to exist in, and a sheet a supplier can work from. Which version goes where, how much space to leave around it, what not to do to it. We want to hand that sheet to a wax supplier we have never met and never speak to them again. Keep it editable, because the release list changes every season.

Second: the release labels. Our printer has last year's file. We do not, and we never did. Keep the label as it is, change everything on it for this year's twelve casks, and send back something the printer can run, plus one file per cask, named so the bottling hall can pull the right one without opening it.

We have three phone photographs of our own packaging you can use, and if you need one more picture we will pay for it.

On tone: our bottles sit next to bottles at twelve dollars. Restrained, plenty of air, one ink doing the work. If anything in our own list looks wrong to you, say so before you make it.
price_band_and_audience: Bottles 55 to 120 dollars (standard gin 55, cask-strength single malt 95 to 120). Buyer 30 to 55 buying a gift or a considered bottle, plus the merchant deciding whether the bottle earns its shelf facing. The band is load-bearing: at this tier the one-ink treatments read as restraint and heritage, a single deep ink, generous clear space, emboss and wax finishes carrying the value, and a supplier sheet written as instruction rather than advertisement. A twelve-dollar brand would take the opposite answer, louder and higher-contrast, and would not care whether the stencil and foil versions were different drawings. An agent that ships a loud, dense set has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,500 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: A two-person coastal distillery making small-batch gin and cask-strength single malt, sold shop-direct and through independent merchants.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2020, on the Northumberland coast, England. A two-person distillery: Iris runs the still, her partner runs everything else.
brand_identity.about: Coble & Vane is a working distillery on a stretch of the North Sea coast, named for the flat-bottomed fishing boat that once beached below the still house. We release twelve casks a year and nothing we cannot stand behind. The bottle is meant to earn its place on a shelf and in a hand, not to shout across the shop.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers aged 30 to 55 choosing a gift or a considered bottle, and the independent merchant deciding whether the bottle earns its shelf facing. People who read a label closely and reward restraint.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Bottles 55 to 120 dollars: standard gin at 55, cask-strength single malt from 95 to 120. Upper-craft tier, sitting deliberately apart from the twelve-dollar shelf. Value is carried by finish, emboss and wax rather than by loud print.
brand_identity.typography: Display in an engraved-feeling serif with real weight in the caps, set with generous letter spacing. Text in a quiet humanist sans for supplier and label copy. The type stays out of the way and lets a single ink do the work.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, dry, unhurried. Written as instruction, not advertisement. Example line: "One ink, plenty of air, and nothing shiny. If our own list looks wrong to you, say so before you make it."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The house mark was drawn six years ago by an illustrator who has since moved abroad and cannot be reached. It survives only as a full-colour illustration flattened to a single PNG. There are no vector files, no one-ink versions, and no supplier guidance sheet. Every single-colour version a supplier has ever received was improvised from that one file, and no two have matched.
brand_identity.values: Restraint and honesty. One deep ink, generous clear space, and finishes that carry the value instead of the print. Say plainly what a version can and cannot do.

assets_supplied.name: house_mark_colour.png (3600 x 3600)
assets_supplied.kind: The distillery's only surviving copy of its mark: a full-colour engraved-style illustration of a beached coble under a rope ring carrying the two family names, flattened to PNG.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our mark as she drew it. This file is all we have and there is nobody to ask for anything else."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. Hull, sail and water are shaded with fine engraved cross-hatch and the rope ring is two interleaved strands in two closely related inks, so the mark's weight comes from tone rather than line and reducing it to one ink is a decision about what stops existing rather than a trace. It was also composited over a warm laid-paper texture and flattened, so any preparation separating ink from ground by lightness takes part of the paper with it.

assets_supplied.name: cask_labels_2025_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF for last season's cask release labels, from a real page layout with embedded font subsets, one page, 210 x 148 mm.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What Redgate ran for us last year. We have never opened it. Keep the label as it is."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two structural facts nobody at the distillery could tell you and nothing in the PDF announces. The page is not a label, it is the die sheet: front and back labels sit side by side because that is how the cutter is set, so one cask is one sheet carrying two dissimilar labels. And the back label's whole copy block came across as one continuous story rather than addressable lines, with the mapping readout silently omitting one run so every offset past it is short while the validator still reports the mapping valid.

assets_supplied.name: cask_release_2026.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The cask book export, one row per release: cask number, expression name, strength, filling date, bottling date, outturn, volume, distilled-at line, photo filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This year's twelve, straight out of the cask book. Iris writes the expression names herself and they go on the label as written."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. Three casks were re-numbered after a re-racking last autumn and the photo column still carries their old numbers, so three rows bind a photograph of the wrong cask while every filename resolves. And the filling and bottling dates are transposed on two adjacent rows, settleable only by reading them against the strength and outturn rather than by validating the file.

assets_supplied.name: packaging_shots/ (3 frames, 4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Phone photographs the founders took of their own packaging: a wax seal over a bottle neck, a stencilled crate end, and a cap from above.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our own wax, our own crate, our own cap. Use these on the sheet so a supplier can see what we mean."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. Wax and cap were shot indoors under a warm work lamp and the crate outdoors in flat daylight, so the three will not sit together without different corrections. And the wax seal is deep oxblood on near-black glass, so its shadowed lower rim and the glass share luminance and a subject knockout returns success while quietly eating the bottom of the seal.

assets_supplied.name: supplier_emails.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Four forwarded messages from a wax supplier, a stencil cutter, a closure maker and the printer, each saying what they need and what went wrong last time.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the four of them have actually asked us for. This is the mess we want to stop having."

assets_supplied.name: house_words.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Half a page of tone and colour language from Iris, with no hex values and no measurements.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we talk about the work. Salt, iron, cold light, nothing shiny."

acceptance_bar: The mark comes back as artwork a supplier can place at any size, transparent, with nothing behind it, and no white or black box appears on a coloured ground.
Whatever ground and size a variant is specified for, it still reads as our mark there. A version that closes up, breaks up or blobs at its specified size is a rejected file.
A version claimed as one ink is genuinely one ink, not a family of near-identical inks.
Enclosed shapes stay enclosed. A filled rope ring, a closed sail gap or a closed letter counter is a rejected file.
The variants read as versions of ONE mark laid out together, not four different drawings of a boat.
No file is larger than the frame it came from, and the note lists every picture resized and by how much.

The three packaging photographs read as one set on one sheet: one white point, one warmth, one black point. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named to us rather than shipped at eighty percent.
Nothing is cut out sloppily. A seal or cap with a bitten edge is rejected on sight.

Release labels: one sheet per cask in cask-book order, every line last year's artwork carried present on every sheet, the photograph on each sheet the cask named on it, at real print resolution at the sheet's true trim.
One label file per cask, named so the bottling hall can pull the right one without opening it, and its contents are what its name claims.

The supplier sheet is one working file we can edit ourselves, every canvas at its own size, mark as real artwork and words as live text, plus the source it was built from, in one type system whose family, foundry and weight you name per role.

A written note: what was done to each picture, which version is for which supplier and why, anything in our own list you questioned, and anything you could not do inside the printer's file, told to us before it reaches Redgate.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize, counted here and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_inline_preview, image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, masked and unmasked image_apply_adjustments, image_apply_monochromatic_tint, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, image_remove_background on both routes, image_auto_straighten, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every reduction and raster decision. Turning a tonal colour illustration into one ink is a raster-preparation problem, because the tracing call takes no options at all, so the only lever is what the agent hands the tracer. The same surface brings three phone frames shot under two lights to one house neutral and isolates the seal and cap without biting their edges.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout, merge-template authoring, data merge and print render
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml twice (to read the conversion, then to audit the prepared template), generate_indd_mapping_prompt as generator and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with additionalImageFiles and recordRange, document_render_layout at resolution 300 with createSeparateFiles and pageRange in N-N form
adobe_surfaces.role: The printed half: the printer's flat die sheet becomes a live merge template with no working file to start from, the cask book becomes the data source, and the run yields the press file, twelve per-cask named sheets and 300 ppi proofs. The only surface that does record per page, and where the shape of the client's own artwork must be discovered rather than assumed.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html for transport, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search(CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The supplier sheet: an A4 instruction page, a landscape application spread and two trade canvases in one export, each root carrying its own canvas size, native and editable with live text and the reduced mark as real vector shapes. A merge template does no free-form layout, so this cannot come off that surface.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend once per role, font_styles for numeric OpenType weights, find_fonts to launder names into canonical PostScript form, get_fontkit_embed_url for one kit consumed through the returned kebab css_stack
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system across every canvas. The recommender refuses to pair, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction against a 55 to 120 dollar band. Numeric weight is non-standard per family, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and one unresolvable name kills the entire kit.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock plus Boards, counted as one surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search(entityScope StockAsset, short generic queries, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: One licensed cooperage frame for the head of the sheet, which the founders cannot shoot before bottling and which is the only IP-clean way to introduce a picture nobody there took, plus the selects board the founders and printer sign off from before the press file is committed.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook before writing markup, settle which half of the commission lands on which surface, and upload every asset through initialize, PUT and finalize.
trajectory.judgement: The split is the first real decision and the brief never states it. Labels are record per page against artwork the client wants preserved; the supplier sheet needs several canvas sizes and must stay editable. Reversing it discards the label or discovers that record per page cannot produce four canvas sizes.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming surface per deliverable, the confirmed tier, and a manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Look at the colour mark at full size and read it as a printing problem rather than a picture: what carries the weight, what is line, what is tone, what is ground.
trajectory.judgement: A mark whose weight comes from cross-hatched tone and two closely related strand inks has no single correct reduction, so what is mark and what is shading must be decided before anything is prepared. Taking the file as a shape to be traced is the fast answer and is not the same as looking.
trajectory.produces: A written reading of the mark: what is structural, what is tonal, what the ground actually is.

trajectory.action: Prepare the mark: an ink-level selection worded against the artwork's own visual properties rather than its substrate, the correct polarity, a crop to the selection's bounds, a first trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full-canvas path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: wording that takes the drawing and not the paper texture, which polarity to hand the tracer, and whether to trace the binary plate or the colour-accurate plate. The tracer takes no options, and a mark carrying an opaque ground path is a picture of a mark with a box behind it.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent first mark with on-light and on-dark colourways, wording and polarity recorded.

trajectory.action: Place the trace at the real sizes it is specified for, on the real grounds it is specified for: cap top, wax seal, crate end, shoulder emboss, and look at it there.
trajectory.judgement: A mark inspected at canvas size has not been inspected. The four applications differ in size, ground colour and polarity, and each changes which parts of the drawing survive.
trajectory.produces: A placement contact sheet at each application size on each application ground.

trajectory.action: Build the variant architecture the applications actually need, each from its own raster preparation rather than from one file rescaled.
trajectory.judgement: The client asked for whatever versions the mark genuinely needs, an invitation to decide rather than an instruction to produce four. Whether a fine and a heavy version are one drawing at two sizes or two preparations is settled by what the placements showed, and the count must be defended.
trajectory.produces: The variant set, the preparation recorded per variant, and the reasoning for the count.

trajectory.action: Triage the three packaging frames on light, level, subject tightness and isolation risk, then level what needs levelling and correct each toward one house neutral with its own parameter set, masking where a whole-frame grade would flatten the wax or grey the stencil ink.
trajectory.judgement: Three pictures of the client's own packaging, but not one set, and one batched call would apply one parameter set to all three. Prompt wording is the whole gate on the masks: naming the substrate pulls the selection to the bottle, naming the material's own properties pulls it to the wax.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note and three graded frames at source scale with a parameter log.

trajectory.action: Isolate the seal and the cap, choosing the route per subject, and inspect each cutout edge at reproduction size rather than at full frame.
trajectory.judgement: A knockout is right for a coherent solid on a separable ground and wrong where subject and ground share luminance, and the wrong route returns success. Route is a per-subject decision made by looking.
trajectory.produces: Isolated packaging elements with the route recorded per subject.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the cask book against the photographs and the founders' words, normalise it into a merge-shaped data file with an image column of bare filenames under the required prefix, upload the graded label masters and build the image map against them.
trajectory.judgement: Rows that validate cleanly can still be wrong, and a re-numbered cask or a transposed date pair is settled only by reading the data against the pictures. The client asked to be told, so repointing their data silently is not the same act as repointing it and saying so.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, uploaded masters, the image map, and a first list of questions for the handover.

trajectory.action: Convert the label PDF, export IDML, unzip it, and read what came across: frame counts, real bounds and page positions, object styles, integer page-item ids, and the true story text reconstructed by concatenating the content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is decided here and the answer is a property of the client's file, not of the plan. Bounds must be read as geometry, because where a frame sits on the page is what tells you what the page is.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, a frame inventory with real ids, bounds and positions, and the reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping against what the conversion exposed, validate it, prepare the merge template, then export IDML from the RESULT, unzip it and grep the story for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence. Nothing instructs this verification and nothing warns if it is skipped, and it is the only place the mapping's real yield is visible before pages exist.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with per-row images bound, render the press file and proofs at 300 ppi, then produce the per-cask single-page files and name each to its cask, verifying identity by opening each file rather than by its position in the returned list.
trajectory.judgement: Merging straight to raster silently drops to screen resolution whatever is asked for, and merging straight to PDF forfeits the per-record branch. Naming twelve files by return order is the fast wrong answer, and it is the failure the bottling hall discovers.
trajectory.produces: The press sheet file, 300 ppi proofs, and twelve identity-verified named single-sheet labels.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the cooperage frame, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, then grade it toward the house neutral and lay it beside the packaging set.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing a frame whose light can be brought to the house neutral rather than the prettiest thumbnail. A warm cellar frame and a cold one are equally attractive at 240 pixels and only one will sit with the three.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale frame, graded, judged in or out with the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.surface: Adobe Fonts and Adobe Express, HTML authoring
trajectory.action: Build one kit (recommend per role, pull style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name), then author one self-contained HTML with four roots at four canvas sizes, base64-inline every photograph, place each mark variant as inline vector in an explicitly sized top-left anchored wrapper, declare family and weight on every text element, upload by the allowed-host route, run the readiness check and export. Verify through both channels: resolve the rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per-canvas markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Numeric weight cannot be inferred from a style name and the CSS must use the returned kebab stack. In the export, a photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, weight is not inherited from markup semantics, a right-anchored auto-sized wrapper collapses off the artboard, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed-size set. Every drop returns success, and the preview shows only the first canvas.
trajectory.produces: One kit with family, foundry and numeric weight per role, a native editable Express document holding every canvas, its durable source HTML, and a per-canvas markup audit.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board and add the graded packaging set, the licensed frame and the label proofs within the per-call cap, treating a partial success as partial and re-sending only the entries named as failed. Then write the handover.
trajectory.judgement: What to escalate versus what to fix silently. The note must be specific enough that a wax supplier who never speaks to anybody picks the right file, and honest enough that anything undeliverable inside the printer's artwork is named before the file reaches Redgate.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable selects board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover the acceptance bar requires.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What this illustration becomes when reduced to one ink, judged where it will be used. Its weight is carried by fine engraved cross-hatch and by a rope ring drawn as two interleaved strands in two closely related inks, and the tracing call takes no options at all, so the only lever is the raster preparation. Every preparation succeeds and every result is crisp at canvas size. Only at cap size, and only on the oxblood wax and kraft crate rather than on white, does one preparation show the hatch closing into a solid mass while another shows it dropping out entirely and the ring breaking into dashes. Nothing in any response distinguishes the outcomes, and the polarity flip between light and dark grounds changes which strokes survive.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot either, because there is no parameter to reason about: the tracer has no options, so the correct preparation is knowable only by making one, tracing it and looking at real size on the real ground. Nothing states it, since the brief asks for the mark in one ink, lists where it goes, never mentions hatching or stroke weight, and never asks what the safe minimum size is. And the response is not a re-run but a different raster and usually a changed variant architecture.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Produce a genuinely different plate: a selection worded for the structural line rather than the tonal field, a masked flattening of the hatch before tracing, or the colour-accurate fill-then-trace route. Re-trace, re-inject the viewBox, re-strip the opaque path and re-place at each application size on each ground. Then re-take the variant count, because a mark that will not hold at cap size needs a different drawing rather than a smaller copy, and the sheet's structure depends on that answer.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A wax supplier the distillery will never speak to presses a seal from a file whose rope ring has closed into a solid ring and whose hull has gone to a black blob, on a bottle selling at a hundred and twenty dollars, from artwork that looked flawless in every preview.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's file actually is and what it exposes, which arrives only by converting, exporting IDML and reading the frame geometry. The page is not a label, it is the die sheet: front and back labels sit side by side because that is how the cutter is set, so one cask is one sheet carrying two dissimilar labels with different frame counts and different mapping strategies. And the back label's entire copy block came across as one continuous story, with the mapping readout omitting one run so every offset computed past it is short, while the validator reports the mapping valid and the prepare call reports the placeholders created successfully.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Frame granularity and page imposition are properties of a document made by a printer nobody at the distillery has spoken to; they are not parameters and nothing reports them before the conversion, so no ordering reaches them earlier. Nothing states it: the client calls the file the label and says to keep it as it is, a requirement rather than a description of its internals. And it is not a propagation re-run, because the mapping strategy changes shape, from per-frame replacement to ordered offset arithmetic against an independently reconstructed story, planned twice over for two dissimilar halves of one sheet.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the IDML content runs, recompute every offset from that string, plan front and back as two mappings against one row, order rows sharing a page item so positions descend, re-validate, re-prepare, and re-verify by grepping the round-tripped IDML for every placeholder before any page is merged. Then write the sheet-versus-label finding into the handover so the bottling hall is not counting the wrong artefact.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A press run of twelve cask sheets where the front label is perfect, strength and cask number bind correctly, and the filling date and distilled-at line are silently absent from every back label, delivered as finished artwork with every tool having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the importer does to the delivered artwork once it is inside the document. The returned per-canvas markup is the only channel, because the rendition preview shows canvas one and nothing else, so the application spread and the trade canvases can be inspected only as markup. A traced mark arrives as loose ungrouped shapes rather than one coherent object, the opaque full-canvas path rides along with any variant it was not stripped from and shows as a filled box on the oxblood or kraft panels, and a wrapper sized by its contents rather than explicitly collapses and throws the artwork off the artboard edge. Every one of those returns success with no warning.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Normalisation is the importer's behaviour on this construct and there is no read-ahead, and care cannot dodge it either, because the same authoring choice behaves correctly on one canvas and fails on another depending on how the wrapper resolved. Nothing states it: the brief asks for an editable working file with the mark as real artwork and says nothing about grouping, wrappers or canvases. And it is not a propagation re-run, because the answer changes the artwork and the composition rather than the input.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Parse every canvas's returned markup rather than trusting the export, strip the opaque path from every variant that still carries one, re-anchor every wrapper with explicit left, top, width and height, re-author the panels whose marks arrived as scattered geometry, re-run the readiness check and re-export. Where a variant will not hold on a dark panel, re-take the panel rather than shipping a mark with a box behind it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A supplier sheet handed to four suppliers in which the reversed mark sits in a visible opaque rectangle on the wax panel and the crate panel's artwork has run off the canvas edge, on the pages nobody could preview, delivered as the editable file the distillery will work from every season.

deliverables.name: Coble & Vane one-ink mark system
deliverables.spec: The mark reduced from a full-colour tonal illustration to placeable, scalable one-ink artwork with a real viewBox and no opaque ground path, in the variant set the applications require and in on-light and on-dark colourways. Each variant produced from its own raster preparation rather than one file rescaled, the preparation recorded, each verified at the size and on the ground it is specified for. A system with a defended variant count, not four exports of one trace.

deliverables.name: Cask release labels, press sheet plus per-cask named files
deliverables.spec: One sheet per cask in cask-book order, page count equal to release count, rendered at 300 ppi at the sheet's true trim, every line last season's artwork carried present and bound verbatim from the cask book, plus that cask's own photograph. With one single-sheet file per cask, named to the cask and identity-verified by opening it, and 300 ppi proofs. Produced by reverse-engineering the printer's flat PDF into a live merge template, handed back with a record of how it was derived.

deliverables.name: Packaging photography for the supplier sheet
deliverables.spec: Three founder-shot frames taken under two different lights brought to one house neutral (one white point, one warmth, one black point) plus one licensed camera-scale frame graded into the same set, every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame log of corrections and of every resize any tool reported.

deliverables.name: Isolated packaging elements
deliverables.spec: The wax seal and the cap isolated for the sheet panels, each with the isolation route recorded, because a deep seal on near-black glass and a cap on a bench are not the same problem. Edges inspected at reproduction size on the panel ground rather than at full frame, with transparent versions for layering.

deliverables.name: Supplier sheet as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document holding every canvas at its own size: an A4 instruction page, a landscape application spread and two trade canvases. Live editable text in one licensed type system, every mark variant as real vector shapes, every photograph carried as embedded image data. Delivered with the self-contained source it was authored from, which is the durable half.

deliverables.name: Handover note and selects board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording what was applied to each photograph, which variant is for which supplier and on what evidence, the type system by role with family, foundry and actual numeric weight, what the label conversion exposed and the mapping decisions taken against it, every cask-book row questioned, anything undeliverable inside the printer's artwork, and every resize any tool reported. Paired with a persistent shareable selects board with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: The press label file has exactly one page per cask in cask-book order and renders at 300 ppi at the sheet's true trim.
verifiers_auto.how: Count pages in the rendered press PDF against the reconciled release count and check the render resolution and output dimensions against the trim read from the converted document.

verifiers_auto.text: Every field last season's artwork carried appears on both halves of every merged sheet.
verifiers_auto.how: Grep the round-tripped IDML stories for every expected placeholder across both label clusters, then read text off each rendered page against its cask-book row.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered image exceeds its source frame on either axis, and no crop call reported an upscale entry the handover fails to transcribe.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare every delivered file's dimensions against its source frame and check every crop response's tradeoffs array for upscale or downscale entries.

verifiers_auto.text: Every delivered mark variant carries a viewBox and no full-canvas opaque background path.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse each delivered SVG for a viewBox attribute and inspect path index zero for a full-extent rectangle.

verifiers_auto.text: Each variant claimed as one ink resolves to a single fill value rather than a family of near-identical fills.
verifiers_auto.how: Enumerate distinct fill attributes across the paths of each such variant and reject any carrying more than one.

verifiers_auto.text: The exported Express document holds every declared canvas at its own distinct size, every mark variant appears as vector paths rather than a single image, and every photograph resolved to real image data.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide_count and per-slide width and height from the export response, and parse each canvas's markup for path-type shapes at each mark position, placeholder image data, and elements resolving beyond their declared canvas width.

verifiers_auto.text: Twelve per-cask label files exist, each named to a cask and containing the cask its name claims, and the selects board carries the expected item count with no unre-sent failures.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the cask number off each single-sheet file and compare with its filename, never relying on returned order; compare addedEntityIds against the expected count and require failedItems empty.

verifiers_human.text: Each mark variant still reads as the distillery's mark at the size and on the ground it is specified for, with the rope ring and sail gap open and the hull not closed into a mass.
verifiers_human.how: View each variant at its specified reproduction size on its specified ground, including the oxblood and kraft panels, against the supplied colour illustration.

verifiers_human.text: The variants read as versions of one mark laid out together rather than as several different drawings.
verifiers_human.how: View the whole variant set side by side at one size and judge stroke mass, proportion and character as a family.

verifiers_human.text: The three packaging frames plus the licensed frame read as one set on one sheet.
verifiers_human.how: View the delivered photography adjacent at sheet size and judge white point, warmth and black point as a set.

verifiers_human.text: No cutout reads as bitten or sloppy, particularly the wax seal against the bottle glass.
verifiers_human.how: View each cutout at panel reproduction size on the delivered ground, then zoom the seal's lower rim for an eaten edge.

verifiers_human.text: The design answers the 55 to 120 dollar band: restraint, air, one ink doing the work, a sheet written as instruction rather than advertisement.
verifiers_human.how: Review the sheet canvases and label proofs against the price band and audience, and reject a loud, dense, high-contrast answer.

verifiers_human.text: The handover escalates rather than conceals: questioned cask-book rows, the variant reasoning and anything undeliverable inside the printer's artwork are named in writing.
verifiers_human.how: Read the handover against the triage and conversion findings and check each is disclosed with the decision taken.

decision_gates: The surface split: labels to the merge surface because they are record per page against artwork the client wants preserved, supplier sheet to HTML authoring because it needs several canvas sizes and must stay editable.
What in a tonal colour illustration is the mark and what is shading, decided before any preparation is made.
Selection wording: whether the prompt takes the drawing or the laid-paper texture it was flattened over.
Which polarity to hand a tracer that takes no options, and whether to trace the binary plate or the colour-accurate plate.
How many variants the applications genuinely need, and whether a fine and a stencil version are one drawing at two sizes or two preparations.
Whether to strip the opaque ground path and inject a viewBox, which nothing in the chain does and nothing warns about.
Isolation route per subject, when a knockout is right for a cap on a bench and wrong for an oxblood seal on near-black glass.
Whether the cask book matches the photographs, when three rows carry pre-re-racking numbers and two rows have transposed dates and all validate.
Whether repointing a client's own data silently is the same act as repointing it and saying so.
Whether to trust the mapping readout of the client's text or to reconstruct the story independently from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification, when nothing instructs a re-export and grep of the prepared template.
Whether one record is one label or one sheet, and what to tell the bottling hall once that is known.
Whether to name twelve per-cask files by the order they came back or by opening each one.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, and the real numeric weight per family.
Whether the licensed cooperage frame joins the packaging set or reads as bought, and if bought, whether to push it or search again on the light rather than the subject.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these assets into a frontier image model and it returns a picture of a boat in a ring. It fails all three gates. IDENTITY: this is one specific mark drawn for these two founders by an illustrator who has left, and the engagement is that it must survive reduction rather than be replaced; a regenerated mark is a different distillery's logo, pressed by a wax supplier onto every bottle they ship. SPEC: one sheet per cask in cask-book order at the printer's own trim at 300 ppi, every line of last year's artwork bound verbatim from their cask book, twelve separately named label files each containing the cask their filename claims, one-ink variants that are genuinely one ink and hold their enclosed shapes at cap size, and no delivered file larger than its source. A generated image satisfies none of that and cannot be checked against a cask book. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next season is a data change, and a native document with live text and real vector so the founders update the release list themselves. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: is this page a label or a sheet, does this placeholder exist, is the photograph on this sheet the cask named on it, does this ring stay open at fourteen millimetres on oxblood.
doability_proof: All verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account); five surfaces, honestly counted, with image_vectorize in the Photoshop family rather than as an Illustrator surface. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare PDF end to end headlessly is verified (convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template producing a story containing the expected placeholders). One record per page is confirmed for PDF output; per-record named files are confirmed by two order-verified routes (createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop) while multi-record raster order is documented as reversed and is therefore never used for identity; true 300 ppi comes from document_render_layout because outputSpecs.resolution on the merge is silently ignored. THE DIE SHEET IS BUILT TO A VERIFIED SHAPE: a continuous flow with no placed images collapses to one text frame with zero graphic frames, while interleaved images split it into two text frames plus two graphic frames, so a front half carrying mark and photograph beside a contiguous back-half copy block yields exactly the asymmetry the checkpoint turns on. It must be a real font-embedding press PDF from a full engine, since a thin hand-authored PDF fails conversion opaquely. The lossy textContent readout and the validator returning VALID on the resulting wrong offsets are verified live findings. Per-row image merge through an at-prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles keyed to bare filenames is verified; twelve rows here, so the recordRange loop is carried as an explicit fallback. IMAGING: select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, masked apply_adjustments, remove_background on both routes, auto_straighten and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls, as are the substrate-versus-ink prompt asymmetry, the binary non-anti-aliased mask, the mandatory polarity flip before tracing, vectorize taking no options at all, its missing viewBox and opaque path zero, and its explosion into loose ungrouped shapes in Express. Upscaling is handled not asserted: crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard 2x cap and signals it only in metadata.tradeoffs, and remove_background silently downscales oversized inputs. EXPRESS: multi-root export with mixed canvas sizes is verified, mm canvases resolve at 96 dpi, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, and the right-anchored auto-sized wrapper collapse is a verified defect; transport is pinned to the upload route with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold; verification is split because the rendition preview shows page one only; persistence is not assumed, so the deliverable is the document plus the source HTML. FONTS: the chain is verified end to end, and the non-standard numeric weights, the slug-not-PostScript CSS rule and the all-or-nothing kit call are live findings. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only, the orientation filter is broken and never used, licensed downloads are genuine camera scale, and board placements cap at twelve per call with failedItems signalling partial success. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no document_render_vector or document_merge_data_vector, no variable QR, no bleed, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design or create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no generated imagery, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above twenty files.
